title: Fish Genetics & Breeding
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned 200L Fish Genetics and Breeding curriculum: basic genetics (DNA, chromosomes, genes, alleles), Mendelian inheritance principles applied to fish, selective breeding and heritability, hybridization, chromosome manipulation (polyploidy, gynogenesis), sex determination and monosex culture, and genetic diversity/inbreeding concerns in aquaculture broodstock management.

questions.question: The molecule that carries hereditary genetic information in fish, as in all living organisms, is:
options: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)
Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) only
Glucose
Cellulose
questions.correct_answer: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)
questions.explanation: DNA is the universal hereditary molecule that encodes genetic instructions, organized into genes located on chromosomes within the cell nucleus.

questions.question: A gene is best defined as:
options: A segment of DNA that codes for a specific protein or functional RNA product
An entire chromosome
A single nucleotide base only
A type of fish scale
questions.correct_answer: A segment of DNA that codes for a specific protein or functional RNA product
questions.explanation: Genes are discrete DNA sequences that serve as the basic unit of heredity, encoding instructions for producing proteins or functional RNA molecules.

questions.question: Alternative forms of the same gene, which can produce different variations of a trait, are called:
options: Alleles
Chromosomes
Genomes
Ribosomes
questions.correct_answer: Alleles
questions.explanation: Alleles are different versions of a gene occupying the same locus on homologous chromosomes, responsible for variation in inherited traits.

questions.question: An organism's 'genotype' refers to:
options: Its genetic makeup or the specific alleles it carries
Its observable physical characteristics only
Its geographic location
Its total body weight
questions.correct_answer: Its genetic makeup or the specific alleles it carries
questions.explanation: Genotype describes the actual genetic constitution of an organism, as distinct from phenotype, which is the observable expression of those genes.

questions.question: 'Phenotype' refers to:
options: The observable physical or biochemical characteristics of an organism, resulting from genotype and environment
The organism's complete set of chromosomes only
A synonym for genotype
The number of eggs a fish produces
questions.correct_answer: The observable physical or biochemical characteristics of an organism, resulting from genotype and environment
questions.explanation: Phenotype is the expressed, observable trait (such as body colour or growth rate) that results from the interaction between an organism's genotype and its environment.

questions.question: An individual with two identical alleles for a given gene (e.g. AA or aa) is described as:
options: Homozygous
Heterozygous
Polyploid
Haploid
questions.correct_answer: Homozygous
questions.explanation: Homozygous individuals carry two identical alleles at a given gene locus, in contrast to heterozygous individuals, which carry two different alleles.

questions.question: An individual carrying two different alleles for a gene (e.g. Aa) is described as:
options: Heterozygous
Homozygous
Diploid exclusively with no other meaning
Triploid
questions.correct_answer: Heterozygous
questions.explanation: Heterozygous individuals possess two different alleles at a gene locus, one typically inherited from each parent.

questions.question: A dominant allele is one that:
options: Is expressed in the phenotype even when only one copy is present (heterozygous state)
Is never expressed under any circumstances
Can only be expressed when two copies are present
Determines the sex of the offspring exclusively
questions.correct_answer: Is expressed in the phenotype even when only one copy is present (heterozygous state)
questions.explanation: A dominant allele masks the effect of a recessive allele and produces its associated phenotype even in a heterozygous genotype (one dominant, one recessive allele).

questions.question: A recessive allele's phenotype is expressed only when:
options: The individual is homozygous recessive (two copies of the recessive allele)
Only one copy of the allele is present
The individual has three copies of the allele
It is located on a different chromosome from the dominant allele
questions.correct_answer: The individual is homozygous recessive (two copies of the recessive allele)
questions.explanation: Recessive traits only appear in the phenotype when an individual inherits two copies of the recessive allele, since a single dominant allele would otherwise mask it.

questions.question: In a simple Mendelian cross between two heterozygous individuals (Aa x Aa) for a trait with complete dominance, what phenotypic ratio is expected in the offspring?
options: 3 dominant : 1 recessive
1 dominant : 1 recessive
1 dominant : 3 recessive
All offspring show the recessive phenotype
questions.correct_answer: 3 dominant : 1 recessive
questions.explanation: A monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes (Aa x Aa) produces a 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa genotypic ratio, which corresponds to a 3:1 phenotypic ratio favouring the dominant trait under complete dominance.

questions.question: Selective breeding in aquaculture involves:
options: Choosing broodstock with desirable traits (e.g. fast growth) to produce the next generation
Randomly mating any available fish without regard to traits
Preventing all fish from reproducing
Only breeding fish of different species together
questions.correct_answer: Choosing broodstock with desirable traits (e.g. fast growth) to produce the next generation
questions.explanation: Selective breeding is a genetic improvement strategy where individuals showing superior traits, such as faster growth or disease resistance, are deliberately chosen as parents for subsequent generations.

questions.question: 'Heritability' of a trait in fish breeding refers to:
options: The proportion of observed variation in a trait that is due to genetic differences among individuals
The complete absence of environmental influence on any trait
The exact number of genes controlling a trait
The physical location of a gene on a chromosome
questions.correct_answer: The proportion of observed variation in a trait that is due to genetic differences among individuals
questions.explanation: Heritability estimates how much of the phenotypic variation in a population is attributable to genetic factors versus environmental factors, guiding the potential success of selective breeding.

questions.question: Traits with high heritability respond more readily to selective breeding because:
options: A larger proportion of the trait's variation is genetically controlled and thus passed on to offspring
They are entirely controlled by the environment
They cannot be measured accurately
They are always recessive traits
questions.correct_answer: A larger proportion of the trait's variation is genetically controlled and thus passed on to offspring
questions.explanation: High heritability means genetic differences account for most of the observed variation, so selecting parents based on that trait effectively shifts the trait in subsequent generations.

questions.question: Hybridization in fish breeding refers to:
options: Crossing two different species or genetically distinct strains to produce offspring combining desirable traits
Breeding only within a single pure genetic line
The asexual cloning of a single fish
The complete sterilization of broodstock
questions.correct_answer: Crossing two different species or genetically distinct strains to produce offspring combining desirable traits
questions.explanation: Hybridization combines the genetic material of two different species or strains, often aiming to produce offspring exhibiting hybrid vigour or a combination of parental traits.

questions.question: The 'Heteroclarias' hybrid, commercially important in Nigerian catfish aquaculture, is produced by crossing:
options: Heterobranchus species (male) with Clarias gariepinus (female), or the reverse cross
Two different tilapia species only
A catfish with a carp species
A marine fish with a freshwater fish
questions.correct_answer: Heterobranchus species (male) with Clarias gariepinus (female), or the reverse cross
questions.explanation: Heteroclarias is a widely used hybrid catfish in Nigerian aquaculture, produced by crossing Heterobranchus bidorsalis (or longifilis) with Clarias gariepinus, combining fast growth and hardiness.

questions.question: 'Hybrid vigour' (heterosis) refers to the phenomenon where:
options: Hybrid offspring exhibit superior growth, survival, or other performance traits compared to either parent strain/species
Hybrid offspring always perform worse than either parent
Hybrid offspring are always completely sterile
Hybridization has no effect on offspring performance
questions.correct_answer: Hybrid offspring exhibit superior growth, survival, or other performance traits compared to either parent strain/species
questions.explanation: Heterosis, or hybrid vigour, describes improved performance (e.g. faster growth, better survival) in hybrid offspring relative to their parental lines, a common goal of crossbreeding programs.

questions.question: Monosex culture in tilapia farming is practiced mainly to:
options: Prevent uncontrolled early breeding and stunting caused by overpopulation in mixed-sex ponds
Increase the number of fish species in the pond
Eliminate the need for any feeding regime
Reduce the pond's water requirement to zero
questions.correct_answer: Prevent uncontrolled early breeding and stunting caused by overpopulation in mixed-sex ponds
questions.explanation: Tilapia breed prolifically at a young age; mixed-sex culture leads to overcrowding and stunted growth, so monosex (typically all-male) culture avoids this reproduction problem and improves growth uniformity.

questions.question: Male tilapia are generally preferred for monosex culture over females mainly because males:
options: Grow faster and reach a larger market size than females
Cannot survive in pond conditions
Reproduce more frequently than females
Are naturally smaller than females
questions.correct_answer: Grow faster and reach a larger market size than females
questions.explanation: Male tilapia typically exhibit faster growth rates than females, since females divert energy into egg production and mouthbrooding, making all-male culture more productive.

questions.question: Hormonal sex reversal in tilapia fry is commonly achieved by feeding them a diet containing:
options: 17-alpha methyltestosterone during a critical early developmental period
Only plain plant-based feed with no additives
Excess dietary fibre
Table salt exclusively
questions.correct_answer: 17-alpha methyltestosterone during a critical early developmental period
questions.explanation: Feeding tilapia fry a diet treated with the androgen 17-alpha methyltestosterone during the labile period of sexual differentiation induces phenotypic masculinization, producing all-male populations.

questions.question: Manual sexing of tilapia broodstock or juveniles, as an alternative to hormonal treatment, relies on:
options: Visual examination of external genital papillae to distinguish males from females
DNA testing performed by the farmer at pond-side
Measuring the fish's total body weight only
Observing the colour of the water
questions.correct_answer: Visual examination of external genital papillae to distinguish males from females
questions.explanation: Manual sexing involves visually inspecting the genital papilla shape and urogenital opening pattern, which differ between male and female tilapia, though this is labour-intensive and less precise than hormonal methods for younger fish.

questions.question: Polyploidy in fish genetics refers to a condition where an individual has:
options: More than the normal two complete sets of chromosomes
Exactly half the normal number of chromosomes
No chromosomes at all
Chromosomes from only one parent
questions.correct_answer: More than the normal two complete sets of chromosomes
questions.explanation: Polyploid organisms carry extra full sets of chromosomes (e.g. triploid = 3 sets) beyond the normal diploid (2 sets) condition found in most fish.

questions.question: Triploid fish (induced by chromosome manipulation) are commercially valuable in aquaculture mainly because they are typically:
options: Sterile, redirecting energy from reproduction into somatic growth
Unable to survive past the larval stage
Identical genetically to diploid fish in every respect
Always smaller than diploid fish of the same age
questions.correct_answer: Sterile, redirecting energy from reproduction into somatic growth
questions.explanation: Triploid fish are generally sterile because their odd chromosome number disrupts normal meiosis; this sterility prevents energy diversion to gonad development, often resulting in improved growth and flesh quality.

questions.question: Gynogenesis in fish breeding refers to a reproductive manipulation in which:
options: Offspring develop using only the genetic material of the mother, with paternal chromosomes inactivated
Offspring inherit genetic material equally from both parents as normal
Only male offspring are ever produced
Fertilization occurs without any sperm involvement at all, including physical contact
questions.correct_answer: Offspring develop using only the genetic material of the mother, with paternal chromosomes inactivated
questions.explanation: Gynogenesis uses genetically inactivated sperm (often via UV irradiation) to trigger egg development while excluding paternal genetic contribution, producing maternally-derived offspring, sometimes combined with chromosome doubling to restore diploidy.

questions.question: Genetic diversity within a broodstock population is important in aquaculture breeding programs mainly because it:
options: Provides the genetic variation necessary for selective breeding and helps avoid inbreeding depression
Guarantees that all offspring will be genetically identical
Eliminates the need for broodstock management altogether
Has no impact on long-term breeding program success
questions.correct_answer: Provides the genetic variation necessary for selective breeding and helps avoid inbreeding depression
questions.explanation: Genetic diversity supplies the raw material for selection to act upon and protects populations from the negative effects of inbreeding depression, which reduces fitness and productivity.

questions.question: Inbreeding depression in a fish hatchery population commonly manifests as:
options: Reduced growth rate, lower survival, and decreased reproductive performance
Consistently improved disease resistance
Faster growth than outbred populations
No observable effect on the population
questions.correct_answer: Reduced growth rate, lower survival, and decreased reproductive performance
questions.explanation: Repeated mating among closely related individuals increases homozygosity of deleterious recessive alleles, typically reducing growth, survival, fecundity, and overall fitness, known as inbreeding depression.

questions.question: A common management practice used by hatcheries to minimize inbreeding in broodstock populations is to:
options: Maintain and rotate a sufficiently large, genetically diverse pool of unrelated broodstock
Use only two individual fish repeatedly as broodstock for many generations
Avoid recording any pedigree or parentage information
Randomly discard genetic records after each breeding cycle
questions.correct_answer: Maintain and rotate a sufficiently large, genetically diverse pool of unrelated broodstock
questions.explanation: Using a large effective broodstock population size and periodically introducing new, unrelated genetic stock helps hatcheries avoid the cumulative effects of inbreeding over successive generations.

questions.question: In fish, unlike mammals, sex determination systems can vary considerably; which of the following is true regarding fish sex determination?
options: Sex in many fish species can be influenced by both genetic factors and environmental conditions such as temperature
All fish species have an identical XY sex-determination system to humans
Sex in fish is always fixed and never influenced by environment
Fish cannot undergo any form of sex differentiation
questions.correct_answer: Sex in many fish species can be influenced by both genetic factors and environmental conditions such as temperature
questions.explanation: Fish exhibit diverse sex-determination mechanisms, including genetic (XY or ZW systems) and environmentally influenced (e.g. temperature-dependent) pathways, unlike the fixed genetic system in mammals.

questions.question: Marker-assisted selection (MAS) in modern fish breeding programs involves:
options: Using DNA markers linked to desirable traits to guide the selection of broodstock
Physically marking fish with paint for identification only
Selecting fish based on body colour alone
Randomly selecting broodstock without any genetic information
questions.correct_answer: Using DNA markers linked to desirable traits to guide the selection of broodstock
questions.explanation: Marker-assisted selection uses molecular genetic markers associated with traits of interest (e.g. growth, disease resistance) to more precisely and efficiently select superior breeding candidates.

questions.question: A 'strain' in fish genetics typically refers to:
options: A genetically distinct population within a species, often developed or maintained for specific traits
An entirely different species from the original stock
A term used only for hybrid crosses
A synonym for genus
questions.correct_answer: A genetically distinct population within a species, often developed or maintained for specific traits
questions.explanation: A strain is a genetically distinguishable subgroup within a species, such as a fast-growing tilapia strain developed through selective breeding programs like the GIFT (Genetically Improved Farmed Tilapia) strain.

questions.question: The GIFT (Genetically Improved Farmed Tilapia) strain is a notable example of successful application of which genetic technique in aquaculture?
options: Selective breeding across multiple generations for improved growth performance
Gene editing using CRISPR technology
Random, unmanaged interbreeding of wild populations
Cloning of a single individual fish
questions.correct_answer: Selective breeding across multiple generations for improved growth performance
questions.explanation: The GIFT strain was developed through a systematic, multi-generation selective breeding program that significantly improved the growth rate of farmed Nile tilapia over the original wild strains.
